items.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024
items.q: I guess it was Ran Blake who said something about the Supremacy of the Ear

ctx.x: We still have a ways to go though. I’m deep in thought of all of what you’re talking about partly because I’m teaching a master’s pedagogy in jazz course which we discuss a lot of these things and jazz in the institution has blossomed out of the classical institution, therefore they’ve held the reins and had all the rules and had all the space. And they have let us come into their space a little bit. And it hasn’t been the other way around ever. So what you’re describing is what I feel still.
I’ve wondered, in talking with quite a few musicians and trying to remember who — I guess it was Ran Blake who said something about the Supremacy of the Ear. It might

have been his phrase, but it made me think about how can you justify at an institution like you’re in, one famous around the world, if you wanted to spend a lot of time teaching young jazz musicians to use their ear, can you justify that in a curriculum?
